en: The Banaue Rice Terraces use the inclined plane principle, allowing farmers to walk up the steep Cordillera mountains with less effort.
A bamboo timbangan acts as a first-class lever, pivoting on a central fulcrum to weigh vegetables in a local Philippine market.
Jeepney tires have deep treads to increase friction, preventing the vehicle from skidding on wet roads during the rainy season.
Earth's gravity pulls the waters of the Pasig River toward Manila Bay, creating a steady downstream flow during low tide.
The Philippines has large magnetite sand deposits in Cagayan, which are strongly attracted to magnets due to their high iron content.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay converts heat from underground volcanic steam into electricity to power local homes.
Sunlight reflects off the fine white coral sand of Boracay's White Beach, making it appear exceptionally bright to tourists.
The Philippine tarsier uses echolocation, emitting high-frequency sounds that bounce off insects in the dark Bohol forests to locate prey.
A traditional clay palayok absorbs and retains heat evenly, cooking Filipino stews like sinigang slowly over a wood fire.
The giant wind turbines in Bangui, Ilocos Norte, convert the kinetic energy of strong ocean breezes into electrical energy.
Fishermen in Taal Lake use a simple pulley system to lift heavy nets of caught tilapia from their wooden boats.
Rice husks, a byproduct of harvesting palay, contain chemical energy that power plants burn to generate electricity in Nueva Ecija.
